subject.size_in_frame: a fragment crossing the frame — a hand, then a knee, then a bent back; no single part of her is less than a third of frame height and none of her is whole

second_subject.note: pinched between finger and thumb, the size of a crumb in her fingers — still the brightest object in frame, and now absurd.

headroom: none; she is cropped at the top by the frame and above her by the vault. The only air in the picture is at the far left, over the low curtain.
horizon_eyeline: Lens 0.9 m from beside the glass table: the tabletop plane crosses at 0.72 of frame height, now low and small. No eyeline — her face is not in this frame.

layers.fg: her hand and the key, sharp, and the bare glass tabletop she has just lifted it from
layers.mg: her bent back crossing the frame right to left as she hurries
layers.bg: the low curtain and the west wall, glimpsed past her between the parts of her body

gaze.note: she is heading frame left toward the curtain and the little door; her body's direction of travel is the only eyeline the shot has, and the lead room ahead of her is almost entirely blocked by her own moving mass.

balance: Chaotically overloaded on the right by body, with one very small bright object near the centre. The frame cannot contain her and stops trying.
leading_lines: The tabletop edge runs left into the frame and the curve of her back runs the same way above it — two parallel sweeps carrying the eye toward the door she is going to.
eye_first: The key, tiny and gold in an enormous hand, and the size joke is made in that one glance.
constraint_binding: At 2.74 m she can never be framed whole, so the composition is built from fragments in motion. The key is the size of a crumb in her fingers — the scale joke paid off — so the key and her fingertips are at the same focal plane and both sharp, with no insert to help them.
